Rashi on Nedarim 31a:10:1.hebrew: הלוקח כלי מבית האומן לבקרו - אם יפה, יתן לו דמיו, ואם לאו, שיחזיר לו כליו, כמו כלי זכוכית:
Rashi on Nedarim 31a:10:1.english: One who takes a vessel from the craftsman's house to examine it - If [it is] good, he will give him its value, and if not, he will return his vessel to him, such as glass vessels.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:10:2.hebrew: ונאנס מידו - שנשבר, חייב לוקח לשלם לו:
Rashi on Nedarim 31a:10:2.english: And an accident occurs [to it] from his hand - [Meaning] that it broke, [the] buyer is liable to pay him.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:10:3.hebrew: אלמא הנאת לוקח היא - דהנאה ללוקח במקחו יותר משל מוכר, הלכך חייב, דגמר ומקני נפשיה בההיא הנאה שמניחו לבקרו. והוי כנושא שכר ונתחייב באונסין:
Rashi on Nedarim 31a:10:3.english: Apparently, [it is] the buyer's benefit - For the benefit to the buyer in his purchase [is] greater than [that] of the seller; therefore, he is liable, for he resolves and obligates himself through that benefit that [the craftsman] allows him to examine it. And he is like a paid bailee, and becomes liable for unavoidable accidents.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:11:1.hebrew: אבל שוה בשוה - אינו יכול [למכור], ואי ס"ד הנאת לוקח היא, הקונה חפץ, ולא הנאת המוכר, אפי' שוה בשוה נמי יהא יכול למכור, דלא הוי הנאת מוכר אלא הנאת לוקח: תריץ דמתניתין דמשמע שוה בשוה לא:
Rashi on Nedarim 31a:11:1.english: But equal for equal - he cannot [sell]. And if you would think [that] it is the benefit of the buyer — the one who buys an item — and not the benefit of the seller, even equal for equal he should also be able to sell, since it is not the benefit of the seller, but rather the benefit of the buyer. [The Gemara] answers [the difficulty from] the Mishnah, which implies "equal for equal, no":

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:11:2.hebrew: בזבינא דרמי על אפיה - עיסקא בישא דלא קפיץ עליה זבינא, ודומה לו כמי שמונחת על פניו. ועכשיו, כשמוכרה שוה בשוה, הנאת מוכר היא ולא הנאת לוקח; הלכך מוכר בפחות, אבל שוה בשוה לא:
Rashi on Nedarim 31a:11:2.english: To a sale that lies on his face - [This refers to] poor merchandise upon which buyers do not jump, and it seems to him as though it is lying on his face. And now, when he sells it at equal value, it is the benefit of the seller and not the benefit of the buyer; therefore, he may sell [it] for less, but at equal value — no.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:12:1.hebrew: אימא רישא - דההיא, לוקח ביותר, ודייקינן מינה הכי נמי: אבל שוה בשוה לא, אינו לוקח. אלמא הנאת לוקח הוי, דאי הנאת מוכר, אפילו שוה בשוה נמי הנאת מוכר היא ולא הנאת לוקח, ובהכי יכול ליקח מהן, דאכתי לית ליה הנאה בהנהו זביני:
Rashi on Nedarim 31a:12:1.english: Say the first clause - Of that [halakha]: "He may purchase for more," and we infer from it thus as well: but [at] equal [value] — no, he may not purchase. Thus, it is the buyer's benefit; for if [it were] the seller's benefit, even [at] equal [value] it is also the seller's benefit and not the buyer's benefit, and at that [price] he would be able to purchase from them, since he still has no benefit in those purchases.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:12:2.hebrew: ועוד אימא סיפא קונם שישראל נהנין לי - כלומר, שלא יהו ישראל נהנין "לי" — ממני — לוקח בפחות ומוכר ביתר, אבל שוה בשוה לא:
Rashi on Nedarim 31a:12:2.english: Furthermore, say the latter clause: Konam that Jews derive benefit from me - That is to say, that Jews should not derive benefit "to me" [li — meaning, from me]: he may purchase for less and sell for more, but [at an] equal [price] for equal [value], no.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:12:3.hebrew: ואי בזבינא דרמי על אפיה אפילו שוה בשוה - נמי יהא יכול למכור, דהא הנאת המוכר ולא הנאת לוקח היא:
Rashi on Nedarim 31a:12:3.english: And if [it refers] to merchandise that lies upon his face, even [for] equal [value] - he should also be able to sell [it], for this is the seller's benefit and not the buyer's benefit.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:13:1.hebrew: סיפא בזבינא חריפא - בסחורה דקפיץ עלה זבינא, דשוה בשוה הוי הנאת לוקח ולא הנאת מוכר. הלכך, מוכר ביוקר:
Rashi on Nedarim 31a:13:1.english: The latter clause [refers] to a keen sale - [That is,] with merchandise that buyers jump at, where [selling at] equal [value] for equal [value] is a benefit to the buyer and not a benefit to the seller. Therefore, he sells [to him] at a higher price.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:13:2.hebrew: אפילו שוה בשוה נמי - יהא לוקח המדיר, דהא הנאת לוקח היא ולא הנאת מוכר, ולא יהא הך נהנה ממנו:
Rashi on Nedarim 31a:13:2.english: Even [at] equal [value] as well - let the one who imposed the vow purchase [it], for this is a benefit to the buyer and not a benefit to the seller, and this one [the seller] will not be deriving benefit from him.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:1:1.english: From those who rest on Shabbat - From those who observe Shabbat.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:1:2.english: [He is] prohibited from [deriving benefit from] Samaritans - For they likewise observe Shabbat.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:1:3.english: From those who eat garlic - On Shabbat nights.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:1:4.hebrew: אסור בישראל - דישראל רגילין לאכול שום (ב"ק פב.) מפני עונה שמקיימין מערב שבת לערב שבת, ומרבה להם הזרע, כדאמר: אשר פריו יתן בעתו — אלו תלמידי חכמים המשמשין מטותיהן מערב שבת לערב שבת (כתובות סב:):
Rashi on Nedarim 31a:1:4.english: Prohibited [from deriving benefit] from a Jew - For Jews are accustomed to eating garlic (Bava Kamma 82a) because of [the obligation of] marital intimacy that they fulfill from Friday night to Friday night, and [garlic] increases their semen, as it states: "Which brings forth its fruit in its season" [Psalms 1:3] — these are Torah scholars who have marital relations from Friday night to Friday night (Ketubot 62b).

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:1:5.english: And [he is] prohibited from Samaritans - For they also eat garlic on Shabbat nights.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:1:6.english: And [he is] permitted [to benefit] from Samaritans - For they do not ascend to Jerusalem, rather to Mount Gerizim.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:2:1.hebrew: אפי' עובדי כוכבים נמי - אי משמרין שבת, יהא אסור בהן:
Rashi on Nedarim 31a:2:1.english: Even idolaters as well - If they observe Shabbat, he should be forbidden [from deriving benefit] from them.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:2:2.hebrew: אלא - מאי שובתי שבת? אותן דמצווין על השבת, דהיינו ישראל וכותים; הן מצווין על השבת מפני שהן גרים. אבל עובדי כוכבים, אע"פ שמשמרין שבת, אינן מצווין:
Rashi on Nedarim 31a:2:2.english: Rather - What [is the meaning of] "those who rest on Shabbat"? Those who are commanded regarding Shabbat — namely, Jews and Samaritans; they are commanded regarding Shabbat because they are converts. However, idolaters, even though they observe Shabbat, are not commanded [regarding it].

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:3:1.english: And permitted [to derive benefit] from Samaritans, and why? Aren’t they commanded - Also to ascend to Jerusalem.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:4:1.hebrew: אלא אמר אביי - מאי משובתי שבת? מצווה ועושה קתני:
Rashi on Nedarim 31a:4:1.english: Rather, Abaye said - What is [the meaning of] "from those who rest on Shabbat"? It teaches [one who is] commanded and performs.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:4:2.english: In the first two clauses - In [the cases of] Shabbat and garlic.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:4:3.english: Jews and Cutheans are commanded and perform [them] - And [he] is forbidden [to derive benefit] from them.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:4:4.english: And idolaters perform [them], but are not commanded - Therefore, [it is] permitted.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:4:5.english: In this [case] of those who ascend to Jerusalem, Jews are commanded and perform [it], [while] Samaritans are commanded and do not perform [it] - Therefore, he is permitted [to derive benefit] from them.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:5:1.hebrew: שאיני נהנה לבני נח - שלא יהנה מכל בני נח, שכל העולם יצאו מבני נח:
Rashi on Nedarim 31a:5:1.english: That I will not benefit from the descendants of Noah - [Meaning] that he will not benefit from any of the descendants of Noah, for the entire world descended from the descendants of Noah.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:6:1.english: Since Abraham was sanctified - In the portion of the Holy One, Blessed be He.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:6:2.english: They are called - Israel [are called] by the name of Abraham, and not by the name of the descendants of Noah.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:8:1.hebrew: הא איכא ישמעאל - דזרע אברהם הוא, והוא מן העובדי כוכבים:
Rashi on Nedarim 31a:8:1.english: Isn't there Ishmael - For he is the seed of Abraham, and he is of the idolaters.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:8:2.english: Shall seed be called to you - And regarding that seed he vowed.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:8:3.hebrew: ולא כל יצחק - ועשו אינו נקרא זרע יצחק, להכי מותר בעובדי כוכבים:
Rashi on Nedarim 31a:8:3.english: And not all [of] Isaac - And Esau is not called the seed of Isaac; therefore, [one] is permitted [to derive benefit] from idolaters.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:9:1.hebrew: שאיני נהנה מישראל לוקח מהן ביתר ומוכר להם בפחות - כלומר בזול, ונמצא שאינו נהנה מהן:
Rashi on Nedarim 31a:9:1.english: "[If one vows:] I will not benefit from a Jew," he purchases from them for more and sells to them for less - That is to say, cheaply, and thus it turns out that he does not benefit from them.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:9:2.hebrew: שישראל - לא יהו נהנין ממנו; מוכר להן ביוקר, דהשתא אין נהנין ממנו:
Rashi on Nedarim 31a:9:2.english: That Jews - [shall] not benefit from him; he sells to them at a high price, for now they do not benefit from him.

Rashi on Nedarim 31a:9:3.hebrew: ואין שומעין לו - שלא ימצא אדם שיהא שומע לו בדבר זה, שבשביל נדרו מוכר לו בזול ויקח ממנו ביוקר:
Rashi on Nedarim 31a:9:3.english: And they do not listen to him - For he will not find a person who will listen to him in this matter, that on account of his vow [that person] would sell to him cheaply and buy from him at a high price.

Tosafot on Nedarim 31a:1:1.english: One who takes a vow [not to derive benefit] from those who rest on Shabbat is prohibited [from deriving benefit] from Jews and prohibited from Samaritans [Kutim] - For the Samaritans also observe the commandment of Shabbat.

Tosafot on Nedarim 31a:1:2.hebrew: מאוכלי השום אסור בישראל ואסור בכותים - פי': אותן שמצווין לאכול שום מתקנת עזרא בע"ש, וגם הכותים שומרים תקנה דאכילת שום בע"ש. וכה"ג דמפרשין הכא, שר"ל מאוכלי השום מע"ש, תנן לקמן פרק קונם יין וכו' (נדרים דף סג:): קונם שום שאני טועם עד שתהא שבת — אינו אסור אלא עד לילי שבת, שלא נתכוין זה אלא עד שעה שדרך שבני אדם אוכלין שום:
Tosafot on Nedarim 31a:1:2.english: "From those who eat garlic — he is prohibited from a Jew, and prohibited from Samaritans [Kutim]" - Explanation: those who are commanded to eat garlic by the enactment of Ezra on Shabbat eve, and the Samaritans also observe the enactment of eating garlic on Shabbat eve. And similarly to what we explain here — that it means to say "from those who eat garlic on Shabbat eve" — we learned later in the chapter [entitled] Konam Yayin, etc. (Nedarim 63b): "[If one says,] 'Konam garlic that I taste until it is Shabbat,' he is only prohibited until Shabbat night, for this [person] only intended until the time when people customarily eat garlic."

Tosafot on Nedarim 31a:1:3.hebrew: מעולי ירושלים מותר בכותים - שלא היו עולין לירושלים, אלא בהר גריזים היו עובדין:
Tosafot on Nedarim 31a:1:3.english: "From those who ascend [to] Jerusalem... [he is] permitted [to derive benefit] from Samaritans" - For they would not ascend to Jerusalem; rather, they would worship on Mount Gerizim.

Tosafot on Nedarim 31a:2:1.hebrew: אילימא ממקיימי שבת אפילו עובדי כוכבים נמי - פי': אם יש עובדי כוכבים, אסור בהם. וא"ת: מאי קאמר? הא סתם עובדי כוכבים אין דרכם לשבות בשבת, אבל סתם כותים שובתין בשבת! וי"ל דהכי קאמר: אילימא ממקיימי שבת ושובתים בשבת — לא בעי למימר ממצווין על השבת, דא"כ לא הוה מיתסר בכותים, משום דסבירא לן כותים גירי אריות הן ואינם מצווין; אלא בעי למימר מקיימין אע"פ שאינן מצווין. ולכך פריך: מאי איריא כותים? דכיון שסבר שכותים גירי אריות הן, דא"כ העובדי כוכבים בכלל הכותים, ויש מן העובדי כוכבים ששובתים בשבת; ולהכי פריך: אפילו עובדי כוכבים נמי:
Tosafot on Nedarim 31a:2:1.english: "If we say [it means] from those who uphold Shabbat ... even idolaters too" - Explanation: If there are idolaters [who rest on Shabbat], he is prohibited from [deriving benefit from] them. And if you ask: What is [the Gemara] saying? Surely ordinary idolaters do not customarily rest on Shabbat, whereas ordinary Samaritans do rest on Shabbat! One can answer that this is what [the Gemara] is saying: If we say [the Mishnah means] "from those who uphold Shabbat" and rest on Shabbat — it cannot mean "from those who are commanded regarding Shabbat," because if so, he would not be prohibited from [deriving benefit from] Samaritans, since we hold that Samaritans are lion-converts and are not commanded [in the mitzvot]; rather, it must mean those who uphold [Shabbat] even though they are not commanded. And therefore [the Gemara] asks: "Why specifically Samaritans?" Because since [the questioner] holds that Samaritans are lion-converts, if so, idolaters are in the same category as Samaritans, and there are [some] among the idolaters who rest on Shabbat; and therefore it asks: "even idolaters too!"
